# FDG5124

> DO provide an alternative for any member that takes a pointer argument, because pointers are not CLS-compliant.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.8.5 Pointer Parameters.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG5124
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Provide an alternative without pointer parameters for '{0}'

Library only: the reason is CLS compliance, which matters to callers of a framework in other languages. FDG5124 reports an externally visible method or constructor with a parameter whose type is a pointer, a function pointer or an array of either, when every overload of the same name declared in the same type (every constructor, for a constructor) has such a parameter. An alternative with another name, or one declared in a base type, is not seen. Overrides and interface implementations are not reported. Adding an overload changes no existing signature, so the fix is not breaking, but there is no code fix. FDG5102 reports the pointer parameters themselves.

## From the book

```csharp
[CLSCompliant(false)]
public unsafe int GetBytes(char* chars, int charCount,
 byte* bytes, int byteCount);
public int GetBytes(char[] chars, int charIndex, int charCount,
 byte[] bytes, int byteIndex, int byteCount)

// Consider Span<T> / ReadOnlySpan<T> instead of
// (or in addition to) methods that take pointers
public int GetBytes(ReadOnlySpan<char> source, Span<byte> destination);
```
